correctness.rationale: The exact four-slot face predicate excludes all directed cycles (only lengths two and four are possible) and all repeated in/out ports; face vectors are proved by counting. The lexicographic type-block matching is acyclic by the earliest pivot in any closed alternating gradient path. The fresh-tail/pivot-bound simultaneous induction with five extra available indices per stage gives only full-size critical cells for every n>=20. Exact exhaustive finite checks verify 6<=n<=19, with independent path enumeration and complete oriented Hasse DAG checks for n=6,7. The resulting CW model has one 0-cell and only 3-cells and so is a wedge of 3-spheres, with multiplicity fixed by reduced Euler characteristic. No finite experiment is substituted for the unbounded induction.

originality.rationale: Original contribution is the unrestricted n>=7 homotopy classification, not the pre-existing finite n=6 case. Public literature concerns bidirected paths and cycles or directed-forest conflict graphs inapplicable to graphs with directed four-cycles. published-finding corpus closest findings about K_{2,n} Morse or two-matching complexes use different simplices, while its bidirected double-star theorem has a different underlying graph. Accessible historical claims contain isolated n=4,5,6 computations, not the uniform result. No stronger/equivalent accessible statement was found; unindexed prior work remains a risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed or inaccessible prior source could contain an equivalent broad theorem; searches cannot establish priority conclusively.

value.rationale: A complete bipartite graph with two hubs is a canonical dense directed test family, and smaller sizes show mixed-dimensional or torsion homology. An all-n integral homotopy classification with a sharp stability boundary and explicit quartic sphere multiplicity supplies a structural result beyond finite ranks or routine enumeration. The proof introduces a reusable bounded-pivot/fresh-tail discrete-Morse mechanism; no downstream theorem is asserted.
